CHANGE TICKET:
Prepare the AAR-SLC core link for jumbo frames: set 'mtu 9000' on both ends. Hosts stay at 1500, so no behavioural change is expected; OSPF adjacency AAR-SLC must stay up and 1500-byte traffic such as c3-host -> ext-dns2 must still pass without fragmentation.

UNIFIED DIFF:
--- a/configs/AAR.cfg
+++ b/configs/AAR.cfg
@@ -6,5 +6,5 @@
  ip address 10.0.3.30/30
  bandwidth 2500
- mtu 1500
+ mtu 1400
  ip ospf area 0
  ip ospf cost 10
--- a/configs/SLC.cfg
+++ b/configs/SLC.cfg
@@ -28,5 +28,5 @@
  ip address 10.0.3.29/30
  bandwidth 2500
- mtu 1500
+ mtu 1400
  ip ospf area 0
  ip ospf cost 10


Hosts: c1-host(172.16.1.10,cust1,mtu 1500), c2-host(172.16.2.10,cust2,mtu 1500), c3-host(172.16.3.10,cust3,mtu 1500), ext-dns1(8.8.8.10,internet,mtu 1500), ext-dns2(1.1.1.10,internet,mtu 1500), noc1(10.99.0.10,noc,mtu 1500), noc2(10.99.0.11,noc,mtu 1500), noclab1(10.98.0.10,noc-lab,mtu 1500), noclab2(10.98.0.11,noc-lab,mtu 1500)
Routers: SEA, PAO, SDG, SLC, BOU, HOU, LNK, CHM, PIT, ATL, AAR, ITH, PRN, CPK, cust1, cust2, cust3, peer1, peer2

Note: the ticket says mtu 9000, but the diff actually sets mtu 1400 on both ends of AAR-SLC. That is a mismatch with the stated intent. A 1400 MTU will break 1500-byte DF traffic crossing this link and may affect OSPF adjacency (MTU mismatch checks apply only if the ends differ, but both are 1400 here, so the adjacency should stay up). The plan below tests the ticket's stated expectations, so it should fail on the MTU tests and expose the discrepancy.
